DgramSocket.constructor: Create a new UDP socket. `DgramSocket` extends `bare-events`. As a shorthand, `opts` may be given as just the socket type, for example `new DgramSocket('udp4')`.
DgramSocket.addMembership: Join the multicast `group` on `iface`, or on all applicable interfaces if `iface` is omitted or `null`. An empty `iface` is treated as an address rather than a default and is rejected, unlike the empty address accepted by `bind()` and `connect()`.
DgramSocket.address: Returns the address information for the local end of the socket, or `null` if the socket is not bound. A link-local IPv6 address is reported with its zone identifier, for example `fe80::1%en0`, so the value can always be passed back to the socket.
DgramSocket.addSourceSpecificMembership: Join the source-specific multicast `group`, receiving datagrams only from `source`.
DgramSocket.bind: Bind the socket to `port` and `address` and start receiving datagrams. If `port` is omitted or `0`, an available port is chosen automatically. If `address` is omitted or empty, the socket binds to all interfaces; otherwise a non-IP `address` is resolved using the socket's `lookup` option. Addresses may carry a zone identifier such as `fe80::1%en0`, and must be at most `constants.address.MAX_LENGTH` bytes. Binding errors are reported through the `'error'` event rather than thrown. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.close: Close the socket, releasing its underlying resources. Pending sends are settled before the socket closes. A no-op if the socket is already closing or closed, rather than throwing. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.connect: Connect the socket to a remote `port` and `address`, binding it first if it is not already bound. A connected socket sends to its peer by default and only receives datagrams from it. If `address` is omitted or empty, the loopback address is used. Unlike `bind()`, `port` must be between `1` and `65535`. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.connected: Whether the socket is connected to a peer.
DgramSocket.disconnect: Disconnect a connected socket, allowing it to send to and receive from any peer again. Throws if the socket is not connected. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.dropMembership: Leave the multicast `group` on `iface`, or on all applicable interfaces if `iface` is omitted or `null`.
DgramSocket.dropSourceSpecificMembership: Leave the source-specific multicast `group` previously joined for `source`.
DgramSocket.getRecvBufferSize: Get the size of the operating system receive buffer in bytes. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise.
DgramSocket.getSendBufferSize: Get the size of the operating system send buffer in bytes. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise.
DgramSocket.getSendQueueCount: The number of send requests currently queued for sending. Tracked by the socket itself, so unlike the operating-system-backed getters above it does not require the socket to be bound.
DgramSocket.getSendQueueSize: The number of bytes currently queued for sending. Tracked by the socket itself, so unlike the operating-system-backed getters above it does not require the socket to be bound.
DgramSocket.pause: Stop receiving datagrams. Datagrams the operating system has already buffered are delivered once the socket resumes, so pausing applies backpressure rather than discarding them. A no-op if the socket is already closing or closed. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.ref: Ref the socket, preventing the process from exiting while it is open. A no-op if the socket is already closing or closed. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.remoteAddress: Returns the address information for the peer, or `null` if the socket is not connected. The returned object has the same shape as `address()`, including the zone identifier on a link-local IPv6 address.
DgramSocket.resume: Start receiving datagrams again after `pause()`. A no-op if the socket is already closing or closed. Returns `this`.
DgramSocket.send: Send `msg` to `port` and `address`, binding the socket first if it is not already bound. `offset` and `length` restrict the send to a subrange of `msg` and may only be given when `msg` is not an array. If the socket is connected, `port` and `address` must be omitted and the datagram is sent to the peer; otherwise `port` must be between `1` and `65535`, and a non-IP `address` is resolved using the socket's `lookup` option. `cb` is called as `cb(err, bytes)` once the datagram has been handed off to the operating system; without a `cb`, send errors are emitted as `'error'` events instead.
DgramSocket.setBroadcast: Enable or disable sending to the broadcast address. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise.
DgramSocket.setMulticastInterface: Set the interface used for outgoing multicast datagrams. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise.
DgramSocket.setMulticastLoopback: Enable or disable delivery of outgoing multicast datagrams back to the local interface. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise. Returns `flag`.
DgramSocket.setMulticastTTL: Set the IP time-to-live of outgoing multicast datagrams. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise. Returns `ttl`.
DgramSocket.setRecvBufferSize: Set the size of the operating system receive buffer in bytes. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise. The operating system may round `size` up to a minimum of its own.
DgramSocket.setSendBufferSize: Set the size of the operating system send buffer in bytes. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise. The operating system may round `size` up to a minimum of its own.
DgramSocket.setTTL: Set the IP time-to-live of outgoing datagrams. Requires a bound, non-closed socket; throws otherwise. Returns `ttl`.
DgramSocket.type: The address family the socket was created with, or `null` if left unspecified (as is required to later adopt an existing file descriptor via `bind({ fd })`).
DgramSocket.unref: Unref the socket, allowing the process to exit even if the socket is still open. A no-op if the socket is already closing or closed. Returns `this`.
createSocket: Convenience function equivalent to `new DgramSocket(opts, onmessage)`.
isIP: Returns `4` if `host` is an IPv4 address, `6` if it is an IPv6 address, or `0` otherwise.
isIPv4: Returns `true` if `host` is an IPv4 address.
isIPv6: Returns `true` if `host` is an IPv6 address.
constants: Internal state and bind-flag constants, plus `address.MAX_LENGTH`, the maximum length in bytes of an IP address accepted by `bind()`, `connect()`, and `send()`.
DgramMessage: The data accepted by `send()` — a string, `Buffer`, any typed array or `DataView`, or an array of these sent as a single datagram.
DgramRemoteInfo: Describes the sender of a received datagram, passed to `'message'` listeners alongside the message itself.
DgramSocketAddress: Returned by `address()` and `remoteAddress()`. A link-local IPv6 `address` includes its zone identifier, for example `fe80::1%en0`.
DgramSocketBindOptions: Options for `bind()`. `fd` adopts an existing file descriptor instead of creating and binding a new socket, and requires a socket created with `type: null`.
DgramSocketConnectOptions: Options for `connect()`. `port` must be between `1` and `65535`.
DgramSocketEvents: `'listening'` fires once the socket is bound and ready to receive; `'connect'` once it is connected to its peer; `'message'` for each received datagram; `'close'` once the socket has closed; and `'error'` when binding, receiving, or an uncallbacked send fails. As with any `bare-events` emitter, an `'error'` emitted with no listener attached surfaces as an uncaught exception.
DgramSocketOptions: `type` is the socket's address family, `'udp4'` or `'udp6'`; pass `null` to leave it unspecified, which is required to later adopt an existing file descriptor. `ipv6Only` (default `false`) binds to IPv6 addresses only rather than dual stack. `reuseAddr` and `reusePort` (both default `false`) allow several sockets to bind the same address and port, with `reusePort` additionally distributing incoming datagrams between them. `readBufferSize` (default `65536`) sizes the buffer datagrams are read into; it defaults larger than the largest possible datagram, so a smaller value can truncate one, which surfaces as an `'error'` event carrying `EMSGSIZE` rather than silently losing data — the socket keeps receiving afterwards. `recvBufferSize` and `sendBufferSize` (both default `0`, meaning the operating system default) size the underlying OS receive and send buffers, applied when the socket is bound. `lookup` (default the `lookup` export of `bare-dns`) resolves hostnames as `lookup(hostname, { family }, cb)` with `cb(err, address, family)`; the resolved `family` is always derived from the returned address rather than what the resolver reports, so a result that isn't an IP address string is treated as a failed lookup.
DgramError: Datagram-specific errors, thrown or emitted by the methods above, each with a `code` identifying the failure. `DgramError` exposes a static factory method per error code (for example `DgramError.SOCKET_IS_CLOSED(msg)`) that constructs the corresponding error.
